objective: Separate sports data from people and posts: a Stats page with a Seasons tab (a season's champion, standings, leaders and games, narrowed to one team by a small search bar) and a Players tab (a small player search), a page per player, and a Search page that searches accounts and posts only.
acceptance_criteria: The navigation has a Stats item linking to /stats, between Search and the profile item, with an icon and a visible label, and it is marked current on every /stats and /players route; /stats redirects to /stats/seasons.

/stats/seasons and /stats/players are public and render one Stats heading above a tab list with two tabs, Seasons and Players; each tab is a link, the current one carries aria-current=page, the URL alone decides which tab shows, and the browser Back button moves between them.

The Seasons tab has a season picker filled from GET /events/seasons, newest first and selected by default, and the chosen season is kept in the URL (?season=), so a reload or a shared link shows the same season.

For the chosen season and no team, the tab shows the champion and the series result from GET /events/seasons/{season}/champion (or that the season has no champion yet), the standings from GET /events/seasons/{season}/standings as one table per conference with the API's tie-break note, the points, rebounds and assists leaders from GET /events/seasons/{season}/leaders with the qualifying rule the API names, and the season's games from GET /events/games?season= newest first in pages of 50 with a load-more control.

The Seasons tab's search bar matches teams by name or abbreviation as the user types (case-insensitive, over GET /events/teams), offers the matches as a listbox navigable with the arrow keys, and choosing one keeps it in the URL (?team=) and shows that team's record and games from GET /events/teams/{id}/seasons/{season} in place of the league view; clearing the bar returns to the league view.
Every game row and every team in a table links to its page or view: a game to /games/:gameId, a team to the Seasons tab filtered to it.

The Players tab's search bar calls GET /events/players?q= with the trimmed text, debounced, keeps q in the URL, shows each result's name, position and latest team, each linking to /players/:playerId, paginates with a load-more control, and shows an explicit no-results state naming the search.

/players/:playerId is public and shows the player's name as the level-one heading, their attributes (position, jersey, height in feet and inches, weight, birth date, country, school, draft), the regular-season and playoff career lines, a per-season table (season, teams, games, starts, minutes, points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, shooting percentages), and the game log from GET /events/players/{id}/games newest first with a load-more control, each game linking to /games/:gameId; an unknown player renders a not-found message.
On the game page, each box-score player's name links to /players/:playerId.
The Search page searches accounts and posts only: the sports-data filter and its game results are removed from it, the free-text bar is unchanged, and no file under src/ still imports GameFilter.
A new shared Tabs component under frontend/src/components/ui/ renders the tab list, and no existing file under frontend/src/components/ui/ is modified except icons/index.tsx (one icon added).

Every *.module.css file this unit adds or changes contains no hex, rgb(), hsl() or named colour, no px font size, and no outline: none or outline: 0 without a :focus-visible rule in the same file (a static test reads the files from disk).

Every table has a caption and header cells with scope, every table scrolls inside its own container at a 360 px viewport while the page does not, and the PR carries the browser checklist of FrontendUI/verification.md for /stats/seasons, /stats/players and /players/:playerId, with the axe row left to the human.
